                "description": "<p>This block is used to present content side by side in multiple columns, providing a more structured, visually balanced layout.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block's table has multiple columns and rows, with the first row containing only the block name and optional variants.</p>\n           

      <ul>\n          <li>In <strong>subsequent rows</strong>, create as many cells (rows + columns) as needed for your layout. Base the number of columns on how the content is visually organized.</li>\n          <li>Each cell can contain text, images, or other inline elements.</li>\n          <li>As a rule, blocks must not be nested in other blocks.</li>\n      

             <li>Additional rows may be added and must contain the same number of columns as the second row.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p>When rendered, CSS and JavaScript will transform each cell into a column, displaying them in a responsive grid.</p>\n        <p>Look at the source HTML structure and screenshots to determine the natural grouping of          

    content that should become separate columns.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to use</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>When you need to compare or present related content side by side.</li>\n          <li>To organize lengthy copy or various media elements into a more digestible layout.</li>\n          <li>When a balanced, multi-column arrangement         

    supports better readability.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another block</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>If you only need one column or a single piece of content.</li>\n          <li>When each content piece requires its own distinct styling beyond simple columns.</li>\n          <li>If a vertical layout or stacked         

    design is more appropriate for your page structure.</li>\n        </ul>"

                "description": "<p>This block is used to showcase distinct pieces of information in a consistent, card-based layout, each card typically containing an image, a title, and descriptive text.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block’s table has 2 columns and multiple rows, with the first row containing only the      

    block name and optional variants in parenthesis.</p>\n        <p>Each <strong>subsequent row</strong> represents a single card and can include:</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li><strong>Image or Icon (mandatory)</strong> - in the first cell of the row.</li>\n          <li><strong>Text content (mandatory)</strong> - in the second cell of the row. This cell     

     can contain:\n            <ul>\n              <li><strong>Title (optional)</strong> – styled as a Heading.</li>\n              <li><strong>Description (optional)</strong> - below the heading.</li>\n              <li><strong>Call-to-Action (optional)</strong> - linked text at the bottom of the cell.</li>\n            </ul>\n          </li>\n                  

    </ul>\n        <p>When rendered, CSS and JavaScript transform each row into a card, arranging them in a grid or list layout based on available space.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to use</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>To highlight multiple related features, products, or articles.</li>\n          <li>When you want a uniform visual style for          

    items with distinct content.</li>\n          <li>To make a set of clickable, structured elements that are easy to scan.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another block</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>If you need just a single feature or highlight, rather than multiple cards.</li>\n          <li>When your layout requires       

    more complex components or varied styling per item.</li>\n          <li>If a simpler list or table layout better fits the content.</li>\n          <li>If no images are present in the cards, consider the ‘no images’ variant</li>\n        </ul>"

                "description": "<p>This block is used to showcase distinct pieces of information in a consistent, card-based layout, each card typically containing a title and descriptive text.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block’s table has 1 column and multiple rows, with the first row containing only the block name       

    and optional variants in parenthesis.</p>\n        <p>Each <strong>subsequent row</strong> represents a single card and can include:</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li><strong>Text content (mandatory)</strong> - in the first (and only) cell of the row. This cell can contain:\n            <ul>\n              <li><strong>Heading (optional)</strong></li>\n        

               <li><strong>Description (optional)</strong> - below the heading.</li>\n              <li><strong>Call-to-Action (optional)</strong> - linked text at the bottom of the cell.</li>\n            </ul>\n          </li>\n        </ul>\n        <p>When rendered, CSS and JavaScript transform each row into a card, arranging them in a grid or list           

    layout based on available space.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to use</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>To highlight multiple related features, products, or articles.</li>\n          <li>When you want a uniform visual style for items with distinct content.</li>\n          <li>To make a set of clickable, structured elements that are easy to             

    scan.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another block</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>If you need just a single feature or highlight, rather than multiple cards.</li>\n          <li>When your layout requires more complex components or varied styling per item.</li>\n          <li>If a simpler list or table layout better        

    fits the content.</li>\n          <li>If images are present, do not use the ‘no images’ variant</li>\n        </ul>"

                "description": "<p>This block is used to embed a stand-alone video in a page, typically displayed with a built-in player or stylized container.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block’s table typically has 1 column and 2 rows, with the first row containing only the block name and optional variants.</p>\n         

        <ul>\n          <li>The <strong>second row</strong> includes the video source (e.g., a link to a video file or streaming URL).\n            <ul>\n              <li>An optional poster image can be provided in this cell as well.</li>\n            </ul>\n          </li>\n        </ul>\n        <p>When rendered, CSS and JavaScript will display the video      

    in an embedded player, allowing users to play, pause, and control the video directly on the page.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to use</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>When showcasing a single video or a featured piece of audiovisual content.</li>\n          <li>To provide a quick, embedded viewing experience without navigating away from the          

    page.</li>\n          <li>For tutorials, product demos, or marketing materials that rely heavily on video.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another block</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>If you need multiple videos presented in a rotating or gallery format (e.g., Carousel).</li>\n          <li>When you only need to            

    provide a link or reference to external media without embedding.</li>\n          <li>If you require a more comprehensive layout with additional text or media elements.</li>\n        </ul>"

                "name": "Accordion",                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         

                "description": "<p>This block is used to organize content within collapsible sections, allowing users to expand or collapse each section to reveal or hide its contents.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block’s table has 2 columns and multiple rows, with the first row containing only the block name and           

    optional variants.</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>Each subsequent row represents an accordion item as 2 cells:\n            <ul>\n              <li><strong>Title cell (mandatory)</strong> – the clickable title or label for the accordion item.</li>\n              <li><strong>Content cell (mandatory)</strong> – the body text, media, or any additional         

    elements that will appear when this accordion item is expanded.</li>\n            </ul>\n          </li>\n        </ul>\n        <p>When rendered, CSS and JavaScript transform each row into an accordion panel, where clicking the panel toggles the display of its content.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to use</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>When        

    you need to present multiple related topics in a compact format.</li>\n          <li>For FAQ sections or other question-and-answer style content.</li>\n          <li>To help users quickly scan headings and selectively view details.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another block</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>If your         

    content is short and doesn’t require toggling.</li>\n          <li>When you want all details to be visible at once without user interaction.</li>\n          <li>If there are many complex elements that need a more flexible layout.</li>\n        </ul>"

                "description": "<p>This block is used to capture users’ attention with a prominent image, a headline, and an optional call-to-action, typically placed at the top of a page.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block’s table has 1 column and 3 rows, with the first row containing only the block name and optional      

    variants.</p>\n        <p>The single cell in the 2<sup>nd</sup> row should contain:</p>\n        <ol>\n          <li><strong>Background Image</strong> (optional)</li>\n        </ol>\n        <p>The single cell in the 3<sup>rd</sup> row should contain:</p>\n        <ol>\n          <li><strong>Title</strong> (optional) - styled as a Heading.</li>\n             

      <li><strong>Subheading</strong> (optional) - additional text</li>\n          <li><strong>Call-to-Action</strong> (optional) - text with a link.</li>\n        </ol>\n        <p>When rendered, CSS and JavaScript will display this block as a large banner, combining the background asset with text and an optional button.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to          

    use</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>When you need a strong visual statement at the top of a page.</li>\n          <li>To highlight a key message, offer, or brand identity.</li>\n          <li>When you want a clear, high-impact call-to-action above the fold.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another block</strong></p>\n        

         <ul>\n          <li>If the layout requires more detailed content sections rather than a single headline.</li>\n          <li>When page space is limited, and a large banner would distract from other priorities.</li>\n          <li>If you need multiple content elements or a more flexible layout below the main image.</li>\n        </ul>"

                "description": "<p>This block is used to display multiple images or slides in a rotating or swipable format, allowing users to navigate through a series of visual elements with optional text content.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block’s table has 2 columns and multiple rows, with the first row               

    containing only the block name and optional variants.</p>\n        <p>Each <strong>subsequent row</strong> represents a single slide and can include:</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li><strong>Image (mandatory)</strong> - in the first cell of the row, with no other content.</li>\n          <li><strong>Text content (optional)</strong> - in the second cell       

    of the row. This cell can contain:\n            <ul>\n              <li><strong>Title (optional)</strong> – styled as a Heading.</li>\n              <li><strong>Description or Additional Content (optional)</strong></li>\n              <li><strong>Call-to-Action (optional)</strong> – linked text at the bottom of the cell.</li>\n            </ul>\n             

      </li>\n        </ul>\n        <p>When rendered, CSS and JavaScript transform each row into a slide, providing navigation controls (e.g., arrows or dots) for users to move between them.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to use</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>When you have multiple featured images or content pieces you want to showcase in a limited      

    space.</li>\n          <li>To present a dynamic gallery or promotional highlights.</li>\n          <li>When you want to encourage user interaction by clicking or swiping through slides.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another block</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>If you only have one piece of featured content, making        

    rotation unnecessary.</li>\n          <li>When all content should remain visible without user interaction or scrolling.</li>\n          <li>If performance or mobile constraints make slides less user-friendly.</li>\n        </ul>"

                "name": "Tabs",                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                "description": "<p>This block is used to present multiple sections of content within a single container, with each section accessible by selecting its corresponding tab.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block’s table typically has 2 columns and multiple rows, with the first row containing only the block         

    name and optional variants.</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>Each <strong>subsequent row</strong> represents a single tab:\n            <ul>\n              <li><strong>Tab Label (mandatory)</strong> – In the first cell of the row.</li>\n              <li><strong>Tab Content (mandatory)</strong> – the detailed information or media displayed when the tab       

    is selected, in the second cell of the row.</li>\n            </ul>\n          </li>\n        </ul>\n        <p>When rendered, CSS and JavaScript create a tabbed interface, allowing users to switch between content sections by clicking on each tab label.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to use</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>When you want to             

    organize closely related content into discrete, user-selectable sections.</li>\n          <li>To reduce page scrolling by grouping information under labeled tabs.</li>\n          <li>If a concise, interactive UI enhances content discoverability.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another block</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n                

    <li>If your content is brief and doesn’t require multiple sections.</li>\n          <li>When all details need to be visible at once without interaction.</li>\n          <li>If you prefer a simpler layout, such as an accordion or single-column design.</li>\n        </ul>"

                "description": "<p>This block is used to let users search a site’s content by entering a keyword or phrase, returning relevant pages or documents.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block’s table typically has 1 column and 2 rows, with the first row containing only the block name and optional variants.</p>\n      

           <ul>\n          <li>The <strong>second row</strong> contains an absolute URL to the query index to search (e.g., <a href=\"https://word-edit.officeapps.live.com/block-collection/sample-search-data/query-index.json\">https://main--helix-block-collection--adobe.hlx.page/block-collection/sample-search-data/query-index.json</a>)</li>\n        </ul>\n      

           <p>When rendered, CSS and JavaScript will display a search input field and handle user queries, returning matching results based on your site’s query index.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to use</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>When you want to give users a quick way to find specific content across your site.</li>\n          <li>On websites     

     with a large volume of pages or documents that users may need to locate quickly.</li>\n          <li>If you want a straightforward, built-in search experience without custom coding.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another block</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>If your site has minimal or single-page content where            

    searching isn’t necessary.</li>\n          <li>When you prefer an external or more feature-rich custom search solution.</li>\n          <li>If you only need filtered navigation rather than a text-based search.</li>\n        </ul>"

                "name": "Embed (video)",                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     

                "description": "<p>This block is used to embed external video content (e.g., YouTube, Vimeo) directly into your page, providing a simple way to display interactive or third-party media.</p>\n        <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>\n        <p>This block’s table typically has 1 column and 2 rows, with the first row containing only the       

    block name and optional variants.</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>The following row should contain a single cell with a URL to the external content you want to display.</li>\n          <li>Optionally, if the provided URL is for a video, an image can also be provided in the same table cell. This image will serve as the poster for the video.\n                 

    <ul>\n              <li>The image should be placed above the link in the cell.</li>\n            </ul>\n          </li>\n        </ul>\n        <p>When rendered, the CSS and JavaScript will transform each row into an embedded media component, allowing users to interact with or view the external content.</p>\n        <p><strong>When to use</strong></p>\n      

           <ul>\n          <li>When you want to incorporate external videos directly on the page.</li>\n          <li>To enrich your content with dynamic, third-party media.</li>\n          <li>If providing visual or interactive content from external sources enhances the user experience.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>When to consider another            

    block</strong></p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>If your content is purely text or image-based and doesn’t require embedding.</li>\n          <li>When you need more design control or custom styling of third-party media.</li>\n          <li>If you want to avoid external scripts or slow loading times associated with embeds.</li>\n        </ul>"

⏺ plugin:excat:playwright - Run Playwright code (MCP)(code: "\n// Scroll to top first\nawait page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0));\n\n// Wait a moment for scroll\nawait page.waitForTimeout(500);\n\n// Now let's improve the block highlighting - make labels more visible\nawait page.evaluate(() => {\n  // Remove any existing labels to avoid duplicates\n       

                                                     document.querySelectorAll('.block-label').forEach(el => el.remove());\n  document.querySelectorAll('.block-highlight').forEach(el => {\n    el.classList.remove('block-highlight', 'block-highlight-hero', 'block-highlight-default', 'block-highlight-cards');\n  });\n\n  // Add improved styles\n  const             

                                                     existingStyle = document.querySelector('style[data-block-highlight]');\n  if (existingStyle) existingStyle.remove();\n  \n  const style = document.createElement('style');\n  style.setAttribute('data-block-highlight', 'true');\n  style.textContent = `\n    .block-overlay {\n      position: absolute;\n           

                                                     border: 4px solid;\n      pointer-events: none;\n      z-index: 9999;\n      box-sizing: border-box;\n    }\n    .block-overlay-hero {\n      border-color: #dc3545;\n    }\n    .block-overlay-default {\n      border-color: #28a745;\n    }\n    .block-overlay-cards {\n      border-color: #fd7e14;\n    }\n       

                                                     .block-label-overlay {\n      position: absolute;\n      padding: 8px 16px;\n      font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;\n      font-size: 14px;\n      font-weight: bold;\n      color: white;\n      z-index: 10000;\n      text-transform: uppercase;\n                    

                                                     letter-spacing: 0.5px;\n      box-shadow: 2px 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);\n      pointer-events: none;\n    }\n    .block-label-hero { background: #dc3545; }\n    .block-label-default { background: #28a745; }\n    .block-label-cards { background: #fd7e14; }\n  `;\n  document.head.appendChild(style);\n\n  //       

                                                     Function to create overlay for an element\n  function createBlockOverlay(element, labelText, blockType) {\n    const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();\n    const scrollTop = window.pageYOffset || document.documentElement.scrollTop;\n    const scrollLeft = window.pageXOffset ||                             

                                                     document.documentElement.scrollLeft;\n\n    // Create border overlay\n    const overlay = document.createElement('div');\n    overlay.className = `block-overlay block-overlay-${blockType}`;\n    overlay.style.cssText = `\n      position: absolute;\n      top: ${rect.top + scrollTop}px;\n      left: ${rect.left 

                                                     + scrollLeft}px;\n      width: ${rect.width}px;\n      height: ${rect.height}px;\n    `;\n    document.body.appendChild(overlay);\n\n    // Create label\n    const label = document.createElement('div');\n    label.className = `block-label-overlay block-label-${blockType}`;\n    label.textContent = labelText;\n 

                                                        label.style.cssText = `\n      position: absolute;\n      top: ${rect.top + scrollTop}px;\n      left: ${rect.left + scrollLeft}px;\n    `;\n    document.body.appendChild(label);\n  }\n\n  // 1. Hero Block - the main hero section with the background image\n  const heroContainer = document.querySelector('main

                                                      > div:first-child > div:first-child');\n  if (heroContainer) {\n    createBlockOverlay(heroContainer, 'HERO BLOCK', 'hero');\n  }\n\n  // 2. Default Content - the paragraph\n  const paragraphs = document.querySelectorAll('main p');\n  paragraphs.forEach(p => {\n    if (p.textContent.includes('When you trust us

                                                      with your data')) {\n      createBlockOverlay(p, 'DEFAULT CONTENT', 'default');\n    }\n  });\n\n  // 3. Looking at the screenshot, the red border seems to encompass more than just the hero image - it extends down past the hero section.

⏺ plugin:excat:playwright - Run Playwright code (MCP)(code: "\n// Scroll to top first\nawait page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0));\nawait page.waitForTimeout(300);\n\n// Now redraw all overlays with correct positioning\nawait page.evaluate(() => {\n  // Remove all existing overlays\n  document.querySelectorAll('.block-overlay,                               

                                                     .block-label-overlay').forEach(el => el.remove());\n  \n  function createBlockOverlay(element, labelText, color) {\n    const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();\n    const scrollTop = window.pageYOffset || document.documentElement.scrollTop;\n    const scrollLeft = window.pageXOffset ||                    

                                                     document.documentElement.scrollLeft;\n\n    const overlay = document.createElement('div');\n    overlay.className = 'block-overlay';\n    overlay.style.cssText = `\n      position: absolute;\n      top: ${rect.top + scrollTop}px;\n      left: ${rect.left + scrollLeft}px;\n      width: ${rect.width}px;\n        

                                                     height: ${rect.height}px;\n      border: 4px solid ${color};\n      pointer-events: none;\n      z-index: 9999;\n      box-sizing: border-box;\n    `;\n    document.body.appendChild(overlay);\n\n    const label = document.createElement('div');\n    label.className = 'block-label-overlay';\n    label.textContent

                                                      = labelText;\n    label.style.cssText = `\n      position: absolute;\n      top: ${rect.top + scrollTop}px;\n      left: ${rect.left + scrollLeft}px;\n      padding: 8px 16px;\n      font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif;\n      font-size: 14px;\n      font-weight: bold;\n      color:     

                                                     white;\n      z-index: 10000;\n      text-transform: uppercase;\n      box-shadow: 2px 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);\n      pointer-events: none;\n      background: ${color};\n    `;\n    document.body.appendChild(label);\n    \n    return rect.height;\n  }\n\n  // HERO: Find the element that contains the hero      

                                                     background image\n  // The hero image has alt text or is the first large image in main\n  const mainImages = document.querySelectorAll('main img');\n  let heroImg = null;\n  for (const img of mainImages) {\n    const rect = img.getBoundingClientRect();\n    // Hero image should be large and near top\n    if    

                                                     (rect.width > 600 && rect.height > 300) {\n      heroImg = img;\n      break;\n    }\n  }\n  \n  // Find the hero container - the parent that wraps the image and text overlay\n  let heroContainer = null;\n  if (heroImg) {\n    let parent = heroImg.parentElement;\n    while (parent && parent.tagName !== 'MAIN') 

                                                     {\n      const rect = parent.getBoundingClientRect();\n      // Check if this parent has both the image and the \"Fairness\" heading\n      const hasFairnessHeading = parent.querySelector('h3')?.textContent?.includes('Fairness');\n      const hasCardHeading =                                                     

                                                     parent.querySelector('h3')?.textContent?.includes('Job Applicants');\n      \n      if (hasFairnessHeading && !hasCardHeading) {\n        heroContainer = parent;\n        // Don't break - keep going up until we find one that includes cards (then use previous)\n      }\n      if (hasCardHeading) {\n             

                                                     break; // Stop - we've gone too far up\n      }\n      parent = parent.parentElement;\n    }\n  }\n  \n  if (heroContainer) {\n    createBlockOverlay(heroContainer, 'HERO BLOCK', '#dc3545');\n  }\n\n  // DEFAULT CONTENT\n  const paragraphs = document.querySelectorAll('main p');\n  paragraphs.forEach(p => {\n   

                                                      if (p.textContent.includes('When you trust us with your data')) {\n      createBlockOverlay(p, 'DEFAULT CONTENT', '#28a745');\n    }\n  });\n\n  // CARDS\n  const cardHeadings = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('main h3')).filter(h => \n    h.textContent.includes('Job Applicants') || \n                    

                                                     h.textContent.includes('Clinical Investigators') || \n    h.textContent.includes('Global Privacy')\n  );\n  \n  if (cardHeadings.length >= 3) {\n    let parent = cardHeadings[0].parentElement;\n    while (parent) {\n      const containsAll = cardHeadings.every(h => parent.contains(h));\n      const containsHero

                                                      = Array.from(parent.querySelectorAll('h3')).some(h => \n        h.textContent.includes('Fairness')\n      );\n      \n      if (containsAll && !containsHero) {\n        createBlockOverlay(parent, 'CARDS BLOCK', '#fd7e14');\n        break;\n      }\n      parent = parent.parentElement;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return  

                                                     'Done';\n});\n")
